title: Automated Private healthcheck remediation orchestrator and Terraform module updates
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
Implement a lightweight remediation orchestrator + updated Terraform/IaC modules to automatically resolve and document common Private (VPC) deployment healthcheck failures. Goal is to reduce on-call page volume and mean time to resolution for top failure classes while keeping remediation steps auditable and reversible.

Scope:
- Add IDempotent remediation actions (no-change when already healthy) for common healthcheck failures in Private deployments: NLB target unhealthy, KV cache hot loop, agent process crash, disk-space pressure on inference hosts, certificate/KMS rotation failures, rabbit/redis connection errors, and database credential/connection failures.
- Extend Terraform modules to expose remediation-friendly metadata and resource tags, plus a small operator/service that can apply automated fixes via sane defaults (restarts, rolling evictions, reattach targets, terraform plan/apply hooks).
- Provide runbooks with detection->action->verification and automated remediation playbooks for each failure class.
- Ensure changes are gated by feature flags and require explicit opt-in at deployment time.

Architecture proposal (high level):
- Detection: existing healthchecks (private-agent /health, runtime /live and /ready, NLB target groups, Grafana alerts) feed into a Rules Engine (Grafana Alertmanager or homegrown Lambda) that emits a structured alert to the remediation orchestrator.
- Orchestrator: small stateless service (k8s deployment) that records incidents in a central ledger (S3/DB) and executes remediation actions via: (a) Kubernetes API (pod/delete, drain), (b) SSH/SSM to private hosts for safe restarts, (c) call out to a Terraform executor with limited, auditable modules for corrective apply (example: re-register target group).
- Terraform/IaC changes: new module outputs and resources: "redwood_private.remediation_tags", "redwood_private.healthcheck_owner", and optional resource wrappers that permit safe minor fixes (e.g., aws_lb_target_group_attachment replacement) without full infra drift. Module changes designed to be minimal and reversible.

Runbook examples (condensed):
1) NLB target group reports Unhealthy targets
- Detection: CloudWatch metric TargetResponseTime > threshold + ALB/NGW unhealthy count > 0.
- Automated action (opt-in): orchestrator invokes terraform module to re-register targets or re-attach ENIs; fallback: trigger rolling restart of agent pods on impacted hosts.
- Manual steps: curl -v http://<host>:8080/health, kubectl describe pod <pod>, kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-agent --namespace private-redwood
- Verification: cloudwatch "HealthyHostCount" increases to expected, /ready endpoints return 200.
- Rollback: if registration fails or CPU spikes, abort and revert terraform apply with saved plan.

2) Agent KV-cache stuck / memory leak pattern
- Detection: process RSS > 80% or KV-cache eviction spikes + runtime /metrics showing hot loop, alert: KV_CACHE_EVICT_RATE_HIGH.
- Automated action (opt-in): graceful restart of affected agent process with pod lifecycle preStop hooks; if host-level, schedule drained replacement via ASG lifecycle.
- Manual steps: kubectl delete pod <agent-pod> --namespace private-redwood --grace-period=60, check logs: gh link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/1823
- Verification: RSS drops to baseline, request latency returns to normal.

3) Certificate or KMS decryption failures
- Detection: error patterns in logs: "kms:DecryptAccessDenied" or TLS handshake failures.
- Automated action (opt-in): rotate service certificate using terraform-managed cert resource or trigger KMS key policy refresh script stored in secure S3.
- Manual steps: follow Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Private+Cert+Rotation, run: ./scripts/rotate-cert.sh --env private-prod
- Verification: no TLS errors in 15m and health endpoints OK.

Safety and auditability:
- Every automated remediation will create a change-set/plan saved to bucket with metadata (who triggered, why, diff). For terraform-driven fixes, the orchestrator will require 2-step apply: generate plan -> store plan -> apply only when policy allows (auto-apply flag enabled by customer or on-call).
- Rate limits: per-cluster cooldowns and exponential backoff. No automatic escalations that modify IAM or override customer network controls.
- Opt-in model: default disabled. Customers opt-in per-deployment via module flag: remediation_enabled = true and remediation_mode = [audit|auto|manual].

Terraform/IaC module changes (developer notes):
- Add outputs: remediation_tags = {"remediator":"redwood-orchestrator","cluster":"private-prod"}
- Add resource wrappers: aws_lb_target_group_attachment with lifecycle "create_before_destroy = true" and tolerable drift detection label.
- Add a "remediation_role_arn" optional param so orchestrator can assume a least-privilege role scoped to limited actions.
- Keep module changes backwards-compatible; default behaviour unchanged unless remediation_enabled = true.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit and integration tests in infra-ci that spin up a minimal private cluster in the test VPC, simulate failures (chaos job) and assert the orchestrator stops an incident within SLO.
- Staged rollout: internal QA -> partner test clusters -> opt-in customers. Canary on 5% of new private deployments for 2 weeks.

Metrics to monitor (initial set):
- number_of_auto_remediations (by type)
- MTTR_auto_vs_manual
- remediations_failed_rate
- post_remediation_error_rate (5m, 15m windows)

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Use existing Alertmanager vs build small rule engine: trade-off between implementation speed (Alertmanager) and structured alert payloads (homegrown). Decision: prototype with Alertmanager webhooks and add a compact rule adapter to normalize payloads; revisit if signal-to-noise is poor.
- Terraform executor: run 'terraform apply' from orchestrator vs call an external CI runner. We prefer external runner for full plan retention (use GitHub Actions with protected branch and PR created by orchestrator) but will implement a light executor for urgent apply when auto-apply flag is enabled.

Acceptance criteria:
- Minimal orchestrator service created and can execute two remediation types (pod restart, target re-register) in test VPC with audit logs stored.
- Terraform modules updated with remediation flags and optional role ARNs without breaking existing customers.
- Runbooks created and validated by SRE and PM, playbook tests added to infra-ci.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Miguel: draft the initial orchestrator prototype and the TF module diff (PR: infra#XXXX) (in progress).
- Aisha: finalize runbook doc and Confluence page, coordinate SRE review (blocked on infra test VPC quota).
- QA: create chaos test harness to simulate NLB target failures and KV cache memory leak patterns.

Risks:
- Over-eager automation may make changes in customers' networks; mitigation: default off and least privilege role requirement.
- Vault/KMS permissions complexity: requires security review (flagged).
